transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom. My name is Sarah. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Hi Sarah. I hope you can help me. I just got my new bill and it's completely wrong. It's for an absolutely insane amount of money.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh dear, I'm very sorry to hear that. I can definitely look into your bill for you. To do that, I'll need to verify your account for security purposes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could you please start by providing me with your Customer ID number?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yeah, sure. It's CUST-1032.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. And for the final verification step, could you please provide me with the 4-digit security PIN for the account?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It should be 8-7-6-5.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, thank you, Mr. Gonzalez. I've successfully verified the account. Please give me just a moment to pull up your latest bill.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alright, I have the bill in front of me now. I can see your standard Fiber 300 plan charge for fifty-five dollars, but I also see a very large additional charge. The total amount due is... one thousand three hundred fifty-five dollars. Is that what you're seeing?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes! That's it! How on earth is that possible? My bill has never been more than sixty bucks. This has to be a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand your concern. Looking at the line items here, the additional charge of one thousand three hundred dollars is listed under 'International Data Roaming'. Did you happen to travel outside the country recently?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Well, yes, I was in Spain for a week for a family visit, but I was careful. I used the Wi-Fi at the hotel and my cousin's apartment. I barely used my phone data.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I see. Sometimes phones can use data in the background even when you're not actively using them. Let me take a deeper look into the specific usage logs for your trip. This might take me two to three minutes to get the detailed report from the system. May I place you on a brief hold while I investigate?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Fine, but please be quick. I need to get this sorted out. It's really stressing me out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand. I will be as quick as I can. One moment.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Mr. Gonzalez? Thank you so much for your patience.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I'm here. What did you find?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, so I have the detailed report. It shows that your device connected to one of our partner networks in Spain and used cellular data on five separate days, starting on the 12th of last month and ending on the 16th.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: But what was using the data? I swear I wasn't streaming videos or anything like that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's often not one single thing. Modern smartphones have many background processes. Things like automatic app updates, cloud photo backups, email syncing, and even GPS services for other apps can use data without you realizing it.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Even so, thirteen hundred dollars for that? That's more than the plane ticket cost!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I know it's a shock. The charges are based on our standard pay-per-use roaming rate, which is set by our international partners. In Spain, that rate is two dollars per megabyte of data used.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Two dollars per megabyte? Are you serious? That's extortion.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand your perspective, sir. Those are the standard international rates when a specific travel plan isn't active on the account.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: What travel plan? No one ever said anything to me about a travel plan.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We offer Cymbal International Travel Passes. They're an optional add-on that you can purchase before you travel. For example, the pass for Europe gives you a full gigabyte of data for a flat fee of fifty dollars. It's significantly more cost-effective.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Well, why wasn't I told about this? Why isn't that automatic? This feels like a trap.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's an opt-in service, as not all of our customers travel internationally. Our system shows that a welcome text was sent to your device when you first landed in Spain. That message outlines the pay-per-use rates and includes a link to purchase a pass right then and there.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: A text message? I might have gotten it, I don't know, I ignore most of those. You can't expect people to make major financial decisions based on a text they might not even see.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I do understand the frustration, Mr. Gonzalez, and I am very sorry for how this has impacted you. Let me take a look at your account history. I want to see what we can do for you.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You need to do something. I am not paying thirteen hundred dollars.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me see. I can see you've been a valued Cymbal Telecom customer for over seven years, and your account is in excellent standing. You've never had a late payment.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That's right. I've been a good customer.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We certainly appreciate your loyalty. Because of your long history with us and because this seems to be a one-time issue, let me check our policy for goodwill credits. I may need to consult with my supervisor, so I might need to put you on another brief hold. Is that okay?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, fine. Do what you need to do. Just find a solution.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will do my very best. Please hold.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Mr. Gonzalez? Thank you so much for holding. I appreciate your patience.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, what's the news?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I've spoken with my supervisor, and we've reviewed your account and the situation. Given your loyalty and the circumstances, we are prepared to help.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So, the full roaming charge is one thousand three hundred dollars. I know that's a difficult number to see. While the usage is valid and we are charged by our partner network, I have been authorized to apply a one-time goodwill credit to your account.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: A credit? How much of a credit?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can apply a credit for nine hundred dollars.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Nine hundred dollars... so... what does that leave me with?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That would mean you would only be responsible for the remaining four hundred dollars of the roaming charge, plus your regular fifty-five dollar plan fee.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Four hundred dollars... That's still a lot of money for something I feel I shouldn't have been charged for in the first place.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand that, sir. This credit of nine hundred dollars is the absolute maximum I am authorized to provide as a one-time exception to help with this unexpected charge.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: (Sighs) I just don't have an extra $400 lying around right now. Is there anything else you can do?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can't reduce the amount further, but what we can do is make paying it more manageable. We could set up a payment arrangement to split that four hundred dollar balance over a few months, interest-free.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: A payment plan? How would that work?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We could, for example, split it over your next two billing cycles. That would be an additional two hundred dollars on your next two bills.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That's still a bit steep. My bill would be over $250.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand. How about we stretch it out further? We can do it over four months. That would be an additional one hundred dollars per month for the next four bills.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So... my bill would be about $155 for four months, then back to normal?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. Your bill would be your normal $55 plan fee plus the $100 installment.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: (Pauses to think) Okay... I think I can manage that. It's not great, but I can manage it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm glad we could find a workable solution. I truly am sorry for the initial stress this caused. I will go ahead and apply that $900 credit to your bill right now.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The credit has been applied. For your records, the confirmation number for this credit is C-R-D-7-7-2-1-5. That's C as in Charlie, R as in Romeo, D as in Delta, 7-7-2-1-5.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay... CRD77215. I've written it down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. And now, I am setting up the four-month payment arrangement for the remaining $400 balance. This is now active in our system.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So I'll see the first $100 charge on my next bill?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, that's correct. You'll see a line item for 'Payment Arrangement Installment 1 of 4'. Does that all sound correct to you?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, it does. Thank you for sorting that out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course. And to make sure this never happens again, would you like me to quickly walk you through how to disable data roaming on your phone?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, please! I never want to see a bill like this again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Completely understandable. Do you use an iPhone or an Android device?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I have an iPhone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, perfect. It's very simple. If you can grab your phone, I can guide you.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I have it here.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. Please go into your 'Settings' app.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, in Settings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now, tap on 'Cellular'.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Cellular, got it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Then tap on 'Cellular Data Options'.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You should see a switch right at the top that says 'Data Roaming'. Is that switch currently green, or on?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, it is. It's green.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, that's what we need to change. Please tap that switch to turn it off. It should turn grey.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Done. It's off now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Now, your phone will not be able to use data on a foreign network. It will be restricted to making calls, sending texts, and using Wi-Fi. You can turn it back on if you ever purchase a travel pass.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That's good to know. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're welcome. And I do highly recommend checking out the Cymbal International Travel Passes on our website or through the Cymbal Telecom app before your next trip. It's the best way to stay connected affordably.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I will. Lesson learned, I guess. The hard way.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, I am glad I could help make it a bit less painful. I've confirmed the credit is on your account, and the payment plan is all set up.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I appreciate your help, Sarah. I know I was a bit heated at the beginning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not at all, Mr. Gonzalez. It was a completely understandable reaction. I'm just happy we found a resolution. Was there anything else at all that I could help you with today?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, that's everything. You've answered all my questions.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alright then. Well, thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom. We value your business and hope you have a wonderful rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You too. Bye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.
